blocks.text:
# crap4dart configuration for flutter_agent_harness.
# https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart
#
# RATCHET: the CRAP threshold is pinned at the current worst score
# (356.34, `_handleKey` in bin/../tui_repl.dart) — pushes may only make
# the codebase BETTER, never worse. Lower the threshold whenever the top
# offenders are fixed (run: dart pub global run crap4dart analyze).

sources: [lib, bin]

exclude:
  - '**.g.dart'
  - '**.freezed.dart'
  - '**.mocks.dart'
  - 'build/**'
  - 'vendor/**'

crap:
  enabled: true
  # Current max CRAP score in the repo: 12.0 (re-measured whole-tree on
  # the merged-suite lcov, #1234 rework). The card's named offenders DID
  # move — readPasteboardImage 16.32 (split into fake-seam /
  # platform-dispatch helpers), the CC-12 trio (_handleTreeKey,
  # discoverTaskAgents, _rebuild) split into cohesive sub-dispatchers,
  # the four 0%-cov CC-3 methods covered by tests (frontmatter, video
  # endpoint, below-window ingest, provider picker), the named CC-9 tier
  # split, and _listModels (20 @ 0%) covered by the line-mode /models
  # test. But the FIRST real whole-tree measurement (the authoring box
  # had no dart toolchain) shows the 12.0 → 8.0 repin is not earned yet:
  # 137 methods measure above 8.0 — 54 at exactly 12.00 (the CC-3 @ 0%
  # tier + fully-covered CC-12 dispatchers) and 83 at 9.00 (CC-9 @ 100%).
  # Threshold stays at the measured max; the 12.00/9.00 tier is the next
  # ladder card (cover the CC-3@0% half, split the CC-12 dispatchers,
  # then the threshold follows down to 8.0). Only down from here.
  threshold: 12.0
  # _listModels used to hit 20 with 0% coverage (line-mode-only output);
  # covered by test/cli/provider_models_line_mode_test.dart in #1234.

# ─── loc gate (issue #1234, gh-1232 migration) ─────────────────────────────
# The ≤2800-line file guard MOVED from scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_size +
# the ci.yml shell find-exec guards onto crap4dart's `loc` gate (0.11.0,
# maintainer-confirmed wc -l semantics). Enforced whole-tree on every merge
# validation via `crap4dart check --baseline` (CI quality-gates step) and
# staged files in the pre-commit hook — no staged-scoping escape, no
# hook-dependence, merge-bot merges included. max_lines only DOWN;
# app_localizations.dart is gen-l10n OUTPUT (no .g.dart suffix) — excluded,
# not baselined.

coverage:
  # scripts/pre-commit regenerates this (dart test --coverage) right
  # before the CRAP step runs.
  lcov_path: coverage/lcov.info
  required: true
  branch_coverage: true
  # crap4dart 0.9.5 flipped the run_tests default to true — a bare
  # `analyze`/`check` would silently re-run the whole core suite first.
  # Coverage is regenerated explicitly (pre-commit hook, CI shard merge);
  # do not pay for it twice.
  run_tests: false

# ─── Gates (issue #447) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 0.9.5 default-enables ALL built-in gates; only broken_goldens is
# enforced here, everything else is disabled explicitly so a bare
# `check --staged` (pre-commit, core-only #433 split) means exactly the
# pixel gate. The flutter_app goldens live in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
gates:
  # Issue #1234: the whole-tree ≤2800-line guard (was stage_size +
  # ci.yml shell find-exec, gh-1232). wc -l semantics, generated output
  # excluded — nothing exceeds 2800 today, so the shrink-only baseline
  # starts EMPTY of loc entries. Scope = the package sources [lib, bin]:
  # 0.11.0 has NO per-gate sources override (gates.loc.sources is a
  # ConfigException — caught by CI on 019ede65), and the top-level
  # sources drive the CRAP census too, so they stay untouched. test/ and
  # example/ are enforced by the companion config
  # crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml (same loc gate, sources [test, example]);
  # the app package's own config covers flutter_app/lib.
  loc:
    enabled: true
    max_lines: 2800
    exclude:
      - '**.g.dart'
      - '**.freezed.dart'
      - '**.mocks.dart'
      - 'vendor/**'
  test_coverage: {enabled: false} # own ≥80% coverage-gate job
  complexity: {enabled: false} # CRAP ratchet above already covers it
  method_size: {enabled: false}
  nesting: {enabled: false}
  class_size: {enabled: false}
  weight_of_class: {enabled: false}
  unused_code: {enabled: false}
  unused_files: {enabled: false} # follow-up card (issue #1234 §5). Known
    # FPs to exclude when enabling: the conditional-export IO entry points
    # (lib/io.dart, lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart — public barrels whose
    # importers live outside this repo's import graph) and shared pinned
    # data modules imported only from test/ (lib/src/cli/omp_reg_scenarios.dart,
    # issue #810). lib/fanet.dart was the one confirmed-dead hit — deleted
    # in #1234.
  banned_imports: {enabled: false}
  # Type-2 duplication gate (issue #1106, crap4dart 0.11.0). Renamed-clone
  # detection on top of the Type-1 default; the union with the raw pass can
  # only ADD findings, never lose exact copies. severity: warning starts
  # soft — escalate to error once the 13-file triage debt is paid
  # (follow-up, owner-side). The global jscpd <1% guards stay as-is.
  #
  # Two suppression channels with different contracts:
  # - `// crap:ignore` (needs ignorable: true) = a JUSTIFIED structural
  #   twin, suppressed forever, with a one-line reason in the comment.
  # - `.crap-baseline.json` (via `check --baseline`) = LEGACY debt; the
  #   committed snapshot must only SHRINK: after each triage batch re-run
  #   `dart pub global run crap4dart check --save-baseline` and commit the
  #   only-down diff, or the snapshot rots and starts masking shifts.
  #
  # WINDOW (until severity flips to error): the gate never fails a build —
  # new (not-baselined) duplication only surfaces as a `[WARN]` line in
  # `check` output. Enforcement becomes hard exactly when the owner-side
  # escalation lands; from then on any finding outside the two channels
  # fails CI/pre-commit.
  duplication:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    ignorable: true # enables `// crap:ignore` for justified structural twins
    ignore_locals: true # Type-2: rename locals before hashing (API names stay)
    ignore_literals: false # keeps l10n/theme/symbol tables out
    sources: # cross-module scope from #487
      - flutter_app/lib
      - packages/fa_ui/lib
      - packages/fa_llm/lib
  file_naming: {enabled: false}
  magic_constants: {enabled: false}
  test_assertions: {enabled: false}
  folder_structure: {enabled: false}
  external: {enabled: false}
  public_docs: {enabled: false}
  golden: {enabled: false} # flutter-only gate (core is not a Flutter project)
  accessibility: {enabled: false}
  hardcoded_strings: {enabled: false}

  # Pixel gate over core test/ goldens — none exist today, so this is a
  # no-op that guards the future (issue #447 AC: "and core test/ goldens
  # if any appear"). WARNING, same rationale as flutter_app: the 0.9.5
  # detector misses the Ahem-solid-rect and hollow-square classes and
  # false-positives on V-converging shapes; flip to error when the
  # upstream detector fixes land.
  broken_goldens:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    dirs: [test]
    exclude:
      # TUI screenshots, not goldens: amber/yellow text on the dark theme
      # trips the stripe heuristic (measured 14/14 "overflow stripes" —
      # the same yellow-on-dark detector bug the issue documents for
      # apps_panel/panel_dark). Revisit when upstream fixes land.
      - 'test/integration/**'

The guards job runs:
1. `crap4dart analyze` — CRAP ratchet with threshold 12.0, requires coverage/lcov.info (coverage.required: true). CI merges shard lcov into coverage/lcov.info. Locally I don't have that. But CRAP score with no coverage would treat everything as 0% covered → scores skyrocket → ratchet would fail... but coverage required:true would error if missing.
2. `crap4dart check --baseline` — gates: loc (max 280) + duplication (warning severity — never fails) + broken_goldens (warning). Hmm, with severity warning, gates don't fail. But baseline check: `.crap-baseline.json` must only shrink? "the committed snapshot must only SHRINK" — maybe check --baseline fails if baseline entries no longer match or if new findings exist.

What changed in this PR? +2390 lines across 24 files. New files: lib/src/agent/message_cap.dart etc. Possible failure causes:
- A new file exceeding 280 lines? Unlikely with new ~small files.
- CRAP threshold exceeded: a new method with CRAP > 12.0 (with real coverage from shards).
- Duplication gate: new Type-2 clones flagged — but severity warning, never fails.
- The CRAP ratchet `analyze` with the merged lcov: a changed method's CRAP exceeding 12.0.

Also the duplication guard jscpd <1% on lib/ — that's a step in guards too ("Duplication guard (lib/ < 1%)"). New code could push duplication ≥1%.

# contexts (shard 0..3) never report, and branch protection blocks
    # out-of-scope PRs at 27 green checks. The scope fastpass below
    # green-skips the real steps in seconds instead.
    name: Core tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    timeout-minutes: 12
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared changes — shard green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1695
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1695
- **Title**: gh-1680 [GOAL] Adaptive per-model message-cap handling: learn the cap from the error, coalesce + compact on refusal, pre-emptive compaction before the cap (dmtools-factory 01a14b3a wedge no hardcoded provider tables)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1680` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 24
- **Additions**: +2390
- **Deletions**: -47
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T14:37:23Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-19T07:55:45Z

## PR Description

Closes #1680
### What changed
gh-1680 adaptive per-model message-cap handling: a provider refusal like `400 messages: array length 2049 exceeds limit 2048` is now classified (`classifyMessageCapError`), the cap is learned per model in `~/.fah/model-message-caps.json` (`MessageCapPolicy`), and the loop heals once — host compaction pass + payload-only coalesce — then retries exactly once. Once any cap is known, compaction also fires pre-emptively on message count (next-request projection), never letting the session wedge in the first place.

### Key decisions
- **One-shot heal** in the response stream (`agent_loop_message_cap.dart` part): learn → `MessageCapRelief` (host compaction) → arm coalesce → retry once; second refusal is terminal, transcript untouched until relief (AC7: JSONL byte-identical).
- **Coalesce is outbound-only**: `coalesceMessagesForCap` merges whole tool-call/result pairs and old turns older than the newest user message into compact carriers; never drops the running turn or mid-pair blocks.
- **Cap-unknown edge (E1)**: no parseable limit → no coalesce target, relief-only retry — and the refusal arms exactly ONE pre-emptive compaction pass on the next request (`ModelCapsStore` pending set, in-memory only, re-armed per refusal, disarmed by a numeric learn).
- **Pre-emptive gate in `AutoCompactor`** rides the existing `CompactionTrigger` slot alongside the token window, so headless gets it for free; CLI wires the policy, relief (structured engine), `/context` caps line, ledger row, and TUI event (emits `compact_phase` + compaction notice, mirrors the over-window relief).
- **Wire**: new `message_cap_repair` event (kind + counts, no text); stream-json filters it as fa-internal; tripwire test extended.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/agent/message_cap_loop_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_store_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_coalesce_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_compactor_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_source_scan_test.dart test/overflow_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_message_cap_test.dart
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[Request refused: 400 array length N exceeds limit M] --> CLS[classifyMessageCapError]
  CLS --> LEARN[MessageCapPolicy.learnFromRefusal → ~/.fah/model-message-caps.json]
  LEARN --> RELIEF[MessageCapRelief: ONE structured compaction]
  LEARN --> COAL[arm coalesce target = cap − margin]
  RELIEF --> RETRY[Retry once]
  COAL --> RETRY
  RETRY -->|refused again| ERR[Terminal error — no loop]
  KNOWN[Cap known] --> GATE[AutoCompactor pre-emptive gate: projected msgs ≥ cap → compact]
```

</details>

### Rework round (PR #1695 review)
- **Split tool pairs survive the newest-user cut**: a tool call whose result answers from the kept tail (or beyond a mid-region steering interleave) no longer merges into a carrier — the group rides verbatim and the pairing repair hoists the result back (content is never dropped).
- **Pre-emptive gate success is two-dimensional**: `_maybeAutoCompact` success now requires the token window AND the message-count gate to be clear, so a token-only pass can't silently re-arm every turn.
- **Config pin**: `models.overrides.<provider>.<modelId>.messageCap` pins a cap that wins over the learned record (`ModelCapabilityOverride.messageCap`); the store's unwired `pin`/`remove` mutation pair is gone in favor of `learnedCapOr(learned, pinned)`.
- **Pathological caps stand down**: `messageCapTriggerReached` requires `cap > margin` — a cap at/below the margin no longer fires the trigger on every turn (the reactive heal still coalesces with its own `max(1, cap − margin)` clamp).

### Known pre-existing failures (verified identical on base 096b36d, not regressions)
- `test/integration/headless_log_file_test.dart` (4), `yolo_rm_critical_e2e_test.dart` (2), `job_board_stability_pty_test.dart` (1): the sandbox leaks `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`/`FA_LOG_FILE` into test children — same failures on base.
- `test/cli/tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` + batched `test/cli` runs: native `malloc_consolidate` abort at runner teardown (sandbox PTY issue); all tests pass — run that file standalone.
- `test/browser_ext` e2e: setUpAll needs a browser fixture not present in this sandbox.

# gh-1680: [GOAL] Adaptive per-model message-cap handling: learn the cap from the error, coalesce + compact on refusal, pre-emptive compaction before the cap (dmtools-factory 01a14b3a wedge; no hardcoded provider tables)

## Description

## Incident & RCA — dmtools-factory session `01a14b3a` wedged forever on JoinGonka `400 messages: array length 2049 exceeds limit 2048`

**Symptom.** In the dmtools-factory session `01a14b3a` (fa 1.0.596, `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` via `gate.joingonka.ai`), the run stopped making progress permanently with:

```
400: {"error":{"message":"400 messages: array length 2049 exceeds limit 2048","type":"api_error"}}
```

The failure repeats every 20 minutes (the session waits on a background job + timers; each heartbeat re-sends the same oversized payload and fails again: 2049 → 2051 → … → 2059 messages). The run can never recover on its own.

### Evidence (session JSONL + fa.log, host of record, 2026-10-18)

1. **The model enforces a hard per-request MESSAGE-ARRAY cap of 2048**, independent of token count. `model_request_summary` records show the message count climbing by 2 per turn (tool call + result) to 2049 by 08:21, with every subsequent heartbeat at +2: 2051, 2053, 2055, 2057, 2059. The first 400 lands at exactly 2049.
2. **The session was token-healthy at the time.** The last successful compaction (07:07, `auto-compact pass 3 fallback=structured·hide-fallback tokens 20023→130354 ok=true`) had reduced tokens to ~130k of a 200k window — well under the token trigger. The message array, however, kept growing because the agent ran ~7 tool calls/minute (bash/read/write every ~10s in fa.log).
3. **fa context management is token-only by design** (`lib/src/compaction/compaction.dart` header: "The pipeline is token-based, never message-count-based"; the mid-turn over-window guard in `agent_loop.dart:1476` measures `estimateRequestTokens` vs `window`). There is no message-count dimension anywhere.
4. **The 400 is not classified as overflow.** `lib/src/overflow.dart` `_overflowPatterns` covers token-based overflow errors ("prompt is too long", "exceeds the context window", "too many tokens", "context length exceeded", …) but has **no pattern for `array length N exceeds limit M`** → `isContextOverflow` returns false. The 400 is also not rate-limit/transient → it is terminal per attempt.
5. **No error-driven context repair exists.** The loop's `over-window relief` (issue #387) and the auto-compactor fire only on TOKEN thresholds. A provider-side context refusal (this 400) is not a compaction/trim trigger — the run wedges.
6. **Compounding factor — compaction judge timeout on the same gateway (issue #515).** At 07:07 auto-compact pass 2 failed: `compaction judge timeout (role=smol, model=zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash @ gate.joingonka.ai, 300s budget)`. The smol judge timed out; the fallback bounds by tokens (`keepRecentTokens`), never by message count — so even a successful compaction cannot pull the array under a message cap.

### Root cause (fixable harness defects)

- **A. No message-count awareness.** The model's message-array cap is not modeled; compaction, the over-window guard, and local-trim are all token-only.
- **B. Overflow classifier misses the cap-400.** `overflow.dart` needs a pattern for `array length N exceeds limit M`.
- **C. A provider context refusal never triggers a self-healing repair.** The pairing-400 repair exists (`agent_loop.dart:1489`, issue #85) but a message-cap 400 does not; nothing coalesces/compacts the array under the cap and retries.

---

## Goal — adaptive per-model message-cap handling: learn the cap from the error, coalesce + compact on refusal, trigger compaction before the cap (v2)

**A run can never wedge on a provider message-count cap: the cap is learned per model from the provider's own error, a cap refusal coalesces and compacts the context, and once learned, compaction fires before the cap is reached — with zero hardcoded provider/model tables.**

v1 of this card modeled `maxMessages` as a per-provider tuning knob. The user's correction: JoinGonka is a **gateway hosting many models**, each with its own limit — the cap is a property of the **model**, not the endpoint, and hardcoding provider/model tables is exactly what must not happen. The cap must be **discovered from the error text and learned per model**, then used as a **message-count compaction trigger**.

## Why this framing (supersedes v1)

- Retracted: `maxMessages` as a per-provider/baseUrl tuning entry — wrong granularity (one gateway, many models) and wrong source (hardcoded).
- Retracted: "pinned cap in the catalog" — the only built-in knowledge is the error-text classifier; the cap value itself is learned.
- Chosen: **learn by example, act pre-emptively**. The classifier recognizes the cap-400 shape (built-in, tiny, provider-agnostic); the specific limit `M` is parsed from the error and stored per model identity `(provider, modelId)`; a subsequent run compacts before the cap instead of after the failure.

## Architecture

```
request → cap-400 "array length 2049 exceeds limit 2048"
   │  overflow.dart classifier (NEW pattern; parses M=2048)
   ▼
learn: store (provider, modelId) → maxMessages=M        [persisted per-model store]
   ▼
repair (reactive): coalesce old tool-call/result pairs → send STRAIGHT to a compaction pass
   → retry once
   ▼
next runs (pre-emptive): before each request,
   messageCount ≥ learnedCap − margin  ⇒  trigger compaction (message-count trigger)
   → request rides a compacted array, never a doomed round-trip
```

- **Cap discovery** — `overflow.dart` gains the classifier for `array length N exceeds limit M` / `messages: … exceeds limit …` (and returns the parsed `M`). Provider-agnostic: any model that emits this shape is handled; the regex is the ONLY built-in.
- **Learned-cap store** — a per-model record keyed `(provider, modelId) → maxMessages`, persisted next to the existing per-provider `model_cache.json` lifecycle (boot-load + background warm-refresh; same file family or a sibling). No provider/model tables in source.
- **Reactive repair (first occurrence)** — on a classified cap-400: **coalesce** the outbound array (merge adjacent tool-call/result pairs and old turns into compact messages — the user's "объединить сообщения"), then **send straight to a compaction pass** (the summary is the real message-count reducer), then retry once. A second cap-400 surfaces the terminal error.
- **Pre-emptive trigger (after learning)** — the auto-compactor gains a message-count trigger in addition to the token trigger: `messageCount ≥ learnedCap − margin` fires compaction BEFORE the request. Additive; the token trigger is untouched.

Invariants:
- Coalesce/compact never drops the newest user message or the system prompt; only whole tool-call/result pairs older than the cut point go.
- The session JSONL is byte-identical — repair is outbound-only (like `rewriteHistoryImages` and the pairing repair).
- The only hardcoded knowledge is the error-text classifier; no provider/model name appears in source.
- A model with no learned cap behaves byte-identically to today.

## Capability surface

| Capability | Subject | Shape | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cap-400 classifier | the provider error string | overflow.dart pattern for `array length N exceeds limit M` (+ variants), exposing parsed `M` | core |
| Learned per-model cap | the model identity `(provider, modelId)` | persisted record → `maxMessages`; boot-loaded; no hardcoded tables | core |
| Reactive repair | the outbound messages array | cap-400 → coalesce + compaction pass → retry once | core |
| Pre-emptive compaction trigger | the outbound messages array | `messageCount ≥ learnedCap − margin` fires compaction before the request | core |
| Coalesce step | the outbound messages array | merge adjacent tool-call/result pairs + old turns into compact messages (pairing-safe) | core |
| Cap notice | the user/UI | a trim/compaction fired by the cap names the cap and the count (no values) | core |
| Config override | a model's learned cap | user can pin/edit a model's cap in config (overrides the learned value) | second tier |
| Hardcoded cap tables | — | exclud…

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)


## General PR Comments

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

🧵 Unresolved review threads — rework armed. This machine-authored PR is reviewed (ai_pr_reviewed) but still has open review threads. The rework leg owns open threads: agent:rework is armed on this PR and the rework runner will work through the threads and push. Validation re-runs automatically afterwards, and once the threads are resolved a fresh re-review is armed (review-threads-resolved).

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-18):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the pre-emptive gate's success return is token-only**

The new `overCap` term correctly fires the pass, but the gate's final verdict a few lines below is still:

```dart
return after <= _effectiveContextWindow;
```

— judged purely on tokens. When the cap dimension triggered the pass and the transcript still rides at/above `cap − margin` after compaction (recent messages can't be hidden), the gate reports success and the CLI sends a still-over-cap request: one doomed provider round-trip per turn until the reactive heal coalesces the retry. The `AutoCompactor` itself already reports `success: ... && !_overMessageCap()`; consider mirroring the message-count check in this return (e.g. `&& !messageCapTriggerReached(_agent.state.messages.length, _modelCaps.learnedCapFor(_agent.state.model))`) so an unfixable-over-cap pass reads as failure instead of silently re-arming every turn.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-18):

💡 **SUGGESTION: second-tier pin API shipped with zero callers**

`pin()`, `remove()`, and `learnedCapOr()` (and the pin-semantics paragraph on `learnFromRefusal`) implement the ticket's "second tier: config override" — but nothing in the tree calls them: no config key, no `/`-command, no host wiring, and the pre-emptive gate reads only the raw learned value. Either wire the override (even minimally, e.g. a `modelCaps` map in config consulted via `learnedCapOr` in `_messageCapPolicy`) or drop the API from this PR and add it with the follow-up that uses it — dead public surface in a fresh module rots fast.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-18):

💡 **SUGGESTION: E1 deviation — cap-unknown models never get the pre-emptive pass the ticket specifies**

The ticket's edge case E1 says: cap error without a parseable number → "the model is flagged cap-unknown → **pre-emptive compaction fires on the next request** (one pass), then retry". This line instead arms no coalesce target, and since `learnedCapFor` returns null for a cap-unknown record, `messageCapTriggerReached` never fires pre-emptively either — a cap-unknown model is healed *reactively* (relief + retry per refusal) instead. That still satisfies the hard requirement (never a wedge), but it diverges from the ticket's specified mechanism: every refusal costs a full refused round-trip plus a compaction pass, forever. Consider either giving cap-unknown records a conservative pre-emptive trigger (e.g. fire on the next request after each refusal, as E1 words it) or noting the deliberate deviation on the issue so the edge case isn't re-litigated later.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-18):

💡 **SUGGESTION: clamp `learnedCap - margin` against pathological small caps**

`count >= learnedCap - margin` is unclamped: a learned cap at or below the default margin of 16 (a provider with a tiny per-request array cap, or a misparse like `array length 4 exceeds limit 8` variants) makes `learnedCap - margin` ≤ 0, so the trigger is **always** true — the pre-emptive pass fires on every turn, can never satisfy its own success criterion, and the session lives in a permanent compact-every-turn state. The coalesce target a few lines later in the heal already clamps (`max(1, learned - kMessageCapDefaultMargin)`); mirror that here (e.g. trigger at `max(1, learnedCap - margin)` or treat caps under the fixed overhead as E2 "nothing droppable → terminal + notice" per the ticket).

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-18):

💡 **SUGGESTION: PR description overstates the CLI surface — please align it with the diff**

Three claims in the PR description don't match the code, which will mislead the next reader/reviewer:

1. **Store filename**: the description (and issue title trail) says `~/.fah/model-message-caps.json`; the code and doc comments use `~/.fah/model_caps.json` (`_loadModelCaps`/`_persistModelCaps`).
2. **`/context` caps line**: there is no `/context` command in the CLI (and no caps line was added anywhere) — the claim "CLI wires … `/context` caps line" is unimplemented.
3. **"TUI event (emits `compact_phase` + compaction notice)"**: no `compact_phase` event exists anywhere in the tree; the actual TUI mirroring is `_pushBusyPhase('Compacting context…')` plus the dim `[message cap] …` writeln — worth describing as such.

The "ledger row" does exist (the `fa.log` diagnostic in `_persistEventLiveness`), so that part is fine. A description edit is enough — no code change needed for this one.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-19):

Fixed in `lib/src/agent/message_cap.dart` — `coalesceMessagesForCap` no longer
treats a tool call whose result answers from beyond the newest-user cut as a
mergeable solo unit. When the pairing scan hits a non-matching message before
every call is answered, the whole group rides the payload **verbatim** (the
displaced results are hoisted out of the droppable region, and the pairing
repair places any far-side tail result back next to its call). The old behavior
merged the call into a `[coalesced …]` carrier, so the repair pass dropped the
far-side result as an orphan and the tool output silently disappeared.

Regression tests in `test/agent/message_cap_coalesce_test.dart`:

- **cut probe** — `[call c1, user steer, result c1]` with `target=2`: the call
  stays verbatim and the result survives with its content intact (previously
  dropped; only a synthesized placeholder remained).
- **mid-region interleave** — `[user older, call c1, user steer, result c1,
  user newest]`: the pair stays verbatim too.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-19):

Fixed in `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart`:

- The message-count gate is now a single shared helper
  `_messageCapGateReached()` used by both `_maybeAutoCompact` and
  `_capResumedContext` — the known-cap pre-emptive trigger **or** the one-shot
  E1 pass a cap-unknown refusal armed (consumed via
  `ModelCapsStore.takePremptivePass`, so it fires exactly once per refusal and
  a fresh refusal re-arms it).
- `_maybeAutoCompact` success now requires BOTH dimensions:
  `after <= _effectiveContextWindow && !overCap` — a pass that only shrinks
  tokens while the count still trips the gate is not a success, so the caller
  retries relief and the funnel reports exhaustion instead of silently

# crap4dart configuration for flutter_agent_harness.
# https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart
#
# RATCHET: the CRAP threshold is pinned at the current worst score

blocks.text:
# crap4dart configuration for flutter_agent_harness.
# https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart
#
# RATCHET: the CRAP threshold is pinned at the current worst score
# (356.34, `_handleKey` in bin/../tui_repl.dart) — pushes may only make
# the codebase BETTER, never worse. Lower the threshold whenever the top
# offenders are fixed (run: dart pub global run crap4dart analyze).

sources: [lib, bin]

exclude:
  - '**.g.dart'
  - '**.freezed.dart'
  - '**.mocks.dart'
  - 'build/**'
  - 'vendor/**'

crap:
  enabled: true
  # Current max CRAP score in the repo: 12.0 (re-measured whole-tree on
  # the merged-suite lcov, #1234 rework). The card's named offenders DID
  # move — readPasteboardImage 16.32 (split into fake-seam /
  # platform-dispatch helpers), the CC-12 trio (_handleTreeKey,
  # discoverTaskAgents, _rebuild) split into cohesive sub-dispatchers,
  # the four 0%-cov CC-3 methods covered by tests (frontmatter, video
  # endpoint, below-window ingest, provider picker), the named CC-9 tier
  # split, and _listModels (20 @ 0%) covered by the line-mode /models
  # test. But the FIRST real whole-tree measurement (the authoring box
  # had no dart toolchain) shows the 12.0 → 8.0 repin is not earned yet:
  # 137 methods measure above 8.0 — 54 at exactly 12.00 (the CC-3 @ 0%
  # tier + fully-covered CC-12 dispatchers) and 83 at 9.00 (CC-9 @ 100%).
  # Threshold stays at the measured max; the 12.00/9.00 tier is the next
  # ladder card (cover the CC-3@0% half, split the CC-12 dispatchers,
  # then the threshold follows down to 8.0). Only down from here.
  threshold: 12.0
  # _listModels used to hit 20 with 0% coverage (line-mode-only output);
  # covered by test/cli/provider_models_line_mode_test.dart in #1234.

# ─── loc gate (issue #1234, gh-1232 migration) ─────────────────────────────
# The ≤2800-line file guard MOVED from scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_size +
# the ci.yml shell find-exec guards onto crap4dart's `loc` gate (0.11.0,
# maintainer-confirmed wc -l semantics). Enforced whole-tree on every merge
# validation via `crap4dart check --baseline` (CI quality-gates step) and
# staged files in the pre-commit hook — no staged-scoping escape, no
# hook-dependence, merge-bot merges included. max_lines only DOWN;
# app_localizations.dart is gen-l10n OUTPUT (no .g.dart suffix) — excluded,
# not baselined.

coverage:
  # scripts/pre-commit regenerates this (dart test --coverage) right
  # before the CRAP step runs.
  lcov_path: coverage/lcov.info
  required: true
  branch_coverage: true
  # crap4dart 0.9.5 flipped the run_tests default to true — a bare
  # `analyze`/`check` would silently re-run the whole core suite first.
  # Coverage is regenerated explicitly (pre-commit hook, CI shard merge);
  # do not pay for it twice.
  run_tests: false

# ─── Gates (issue #447) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 0.9.5 default-enables ALL built-in gates; only broken_goldens is
# enforced here, everything else is disabled explicitly so a bare
# `check --staged` (pre-commit, core-only #433 split) means exactly the
# pixel gate. The flutter_app goldens live in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
gates:
  # Issue #1234: the whole-tree ≤2800-line guard (was stage_size +
  # ci.yml shell find-exec, gh-1232). wc -l semantics, generated output
  # excluded — nothing exceeds 2800 today, so the shrink-only baseline
  # starts EMPTY of loc entries. Scope = the package sources [lib, bin]:
  # 0.11.0 has NO per-gate sources override (gates.loc.sources is a
  # ConfigException — caught by CI on 019ede65), and the top-level
  # sources drive the CRAP census too, so they stay untouched. test/ and
  # example/ are enforced by the companion config
  # crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml (same loc gate, sources [test, example]);
  # the app package's own config covers flutter_app/lib.
  loc:
    enabled: true
    max_lines: 2800
    exclude:
      - '**.g.dart'
      - '**.freezed.dart'
      - '**.mocks.dart'
      - 'vendor/**'
  test_coverage: {enabled: false} # own ≥80% coverage-gate job
  complexity: {enabled: false} # CRAP ratchet above already covers it
  method_size: {enabled: false}
  nesting: {enabled: false}
  class_size: {enabled: false}
  weight_of_class: {enabled: false}
  unused_code: {enabled: false}
  unused_files: {enabled: false} # follow-up card (issue #1234 §5). Known
    # FPs to exclude when enabling: the conditional-export IO entry points
    # (lib/io.dart, lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart — public barrels whose
    # importers live outside this repo's import graph) and shared pinned
    # data modules imported only from test/ (lib/src/cli/omp_reg_scenarios.dart,
    # issue #810). lib/fanet.dart was the one confirmed-dead hit — deleted
    # in #1234.
  banned_imports: {enabled: false}
  # Type-2 duplication gate (issue #1106, crap4dart 0.11.0). Renamed-clone
  # detection on top of the Type-1 default; the union with the raw pass can
  # only ADD findings, never lose exact copies. severity: warning starts
  # soft — escalate to error once the 13-file triage debt is paid
  # (follow-up, owner-side). The global jscpd <1% guards stay as-is.
  #
  # Two suppression channels with different contracts:
  # - `// crap:ignore` (needs ignorable: true) = a JUSTIFIED structural
  #   twin, suppressed forever, with a one-line reason in the comment.
  # - `.crap-baseline.json` (via `check --baseline`) = LEGACY debt; the
  #   committed snapshot must only SHRINK: after each triage batch re-run
  #   `dart pub global run crap4dart check --save-baseline` and commit the
  #   only-down diff, or the snapshot rots and starts masking shifts.
  #
  # WINDOW (until severity flips to error): the gate never fails a build —
  # new (not-baselined) duplication only surfaces as a `[WARN]` line in
  # `check` output. Enforcement becomes hard exactly when the owner-side
  # escalation lands; from then on any finding outside the two channels
  # fails CI/pre-commit.
  duplication:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    ignorable: true # enables `// crap:ignore` for justified structural twins
    ignore_locals: true # Type-2: rename locals before hashing (API names stay)
    ignore_literals: false # keeps l10n/theme/symbol tables out
    sources: # cross-module scope from #487
      - flutter_app/lib
      - packages/fa_ui/lib
      - packages/fa_llm/lib
  file_naming: {enabled: false}
  magic_constants: {enabled: false}
  test_assertions: {enabled: false}
  folder_structure: {enabled: false}
  external: {enabled: false}
  public_docs: {enabled: false}
  golden: {enabled: false} # flutter-only gate (core is not a Flutter project)
  accessibility: {enabled: false}
  hardcoded_strings: {enabled: false}

  # Pixel gate over core test/ goldens — none exist today, so this is a
  # no-op that guards the future (issue #447 AC: "and core test/ goldens
  # if any appear"). WARNING, same rationale as flutter_app: the 0.9.5
  # detector misses the Ahem-solid-rect and hollow-square classes and
  # false-positives on V-converging shapes; flip to error when the
  # upstream detector fixes land.
  broken_goldens:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    dirs: [test]
    exclude:
      # TUI screenshots, not goldens: amber/yellow text on the dark theme
      # trips the stripe heuristic (measured 14/14 "overflow stripes" —
      # the same yellow-on-dark detector bug the issue documents for

# contexts (shard 0..3) never report, and branch protection blocks
    # out-of-scope PRs at 27 green checks. The scope fastpass below
    # green-skips the real steps in seconds instead.
    name: Core tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    timeout-minutes: 12
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared changes — shard green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1695
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1695
- **Title**: gh-1680 [GOAL] Adaptive per-model message-cap handling: learn the cap from the error, coalesce + compact on refusal, pre-emptive compaction before the cap (dmtools-factory 01a14b3a wedge no hardcoded provider tables)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1680` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 24
- **Additions**: +2390
- **Deletions**: -47
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T14:37:23Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-19T07:55:45Z

## PR Description

Closes #1680
### What changed
gh-1680 adaptive per-model message-cap handling: a provider refusal like `400 messages: array length 2049 exceeds limit 2048` is now classified (`classifyMessageCapError`), the cap is learned per model in `~/.fah/model-message-caps.json` (`MessageCapPolicy`), and the loop heals once — host compaction pass + payload-only coalesce — then retries exactly once. Once any cap is known, compaction also fires pre-emptively on message count (next-request projection), never letting the session wedge in the first place.

### Key decisions
- **One-shot heal** in the response stream (`agent_loop_message_cap.dart` part): learn → `MessageCapRelief` (host compaction) → arm coalesce → retry once; second refusal is terminal, transcript untouched until relief (AC7: JSONL byte-identical).
- **Coalesce is outbound-only**: `coalesceMessagesForCap` merges whole tool-call/result pairs and old turns older than the newest user message into compact carriers; never drops the running turn or mid-pair blocks.
- **Cap-unknown edge (E1)**: no parseable limit → no coalesce target, relief-only retry — and the refusal arms exactly ONE pre-emptive compaction pass on the next request (`ModelCapsStore` pending set, in-memory only, re-armed per refusal, disarmed by a numeric learn).
- **Pre-emptive gate in `AutoCompactor`** rides the existing `CompactionTrigger` slot alongside the token window, so headless gets it for free; CLI wires the policy, relief (structured engine), `/context` caps line, ledger row, and TUI event (emits `compact_phase` + compaction notice, mirrors the over-window relief).
- **Wire**: new `message_cap_repair` event (kind + counts, no text); stream-json filters it as fa-internal; tripwire test extended.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/agent/message_cap_loop_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_store_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_coalesce_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_compactor_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_source_scan_test.dart test/overflow_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_message_cap_test.dart
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[Request refused: 400 array length N exceeds limit M] --> CLS[classifyMessageCapError]
  CLS --> LEARN[MessageCapPolicy.learnFromRefusal → ~/.fah/model-message-caps.json]
  LEARN --> RELIEF[MessageCapRelief: ONE structured compaction]
  LEARN --> COAL[arm coalesce target = cap − margin]
  RELIEF --> RETRY[Retry once]
  COAL --> RETRY
  RETRY -->|refused again| ERR[Terminal error — no loop]
  KNOWN[Cap known] --> GATE[AutoCompactor pre-emptive gate: projected msgs ≥ cap → compact]
```

</details>

### Rework round (PR #1695 review)
- **Split tool pairs survive the newest-user cut**: a tool call whose result answers from the kept tail (or beyond a mid-region steering interleave) no longer merges into a carrier — the group rides verbatim and the pairing repair hoists the result back (content is never dropped).
- **Pre-emptive gate success is two-dimensional**: `_maybeAutoCompact` success now requires the token window AND the message-count gate to be clear, so a token-only pass can't silently re-arm every turn.
- **Config pin**: `models.overrides.<provider>.<modelId>.messageCap` pins a cap that wins over the learned record (`ModelCapabilityOverride.messageCap`); the store's unwired `pin`/`remove` mutation pair is gone in favor of `learnedCapOr(learned, pinned)`.
- **Pathological caps stand down**: `messageCapTriggerReached` requires `cap > margin` — a cap at/below the margin no longer fires the trigger on every turn (the reactive heal still coalesces with its own `max(1, cap − margin)` clamp).

### Known pre-existing failures (verified identical on base 096b36d, not regressions)
- `test/integration/headless_log_file_test.dart` (4), `yolo_rm_critical_e2e_test.dart` (2), `job_board_stability_pty_test.dart` (1): the sandbox leaks `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`/`FA_LOG_FILE` into test children — same failures on base.
- `test/cli/tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` + batched `test/cli` runs: native `malloc_consolidate` abort at runner teardown (sandbox PTY issue); all tests pass — run that file standalone.
- `test/browser_ext` e2e: setUpAll needs a browser fixture not present in this sandbox.

# gh-1680: [GOAL] Adaptive per-model message-cap handling: learn the cap from the error, coalesce + compact on refusal, pre-emptive compaction before the cap (dmtools-factory 01a14b3a wedge; no hardcoded provider tables)

## Description

## Incident & RCA — dmtools-factory session `01a14b3a` wedged forever on JoinGonka `400 messages: array length 2049 exceeds limit 2048`

**Symptom.** In the dmtools-factory session `01a14b3a` (fa 1.0.596, `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` via `gate.joingonka.ai`), the run stopped making progress permanently with:

```
400: {"error":{"message":"400 messages: array length 2049 exceeds limit 2048","type":"api_error"}}
```

The failure repeats every 20 minutes (the session waits on a background job + timers; each heartbeat re-sends the same oversized payload and fails again: 2049 → 2051 → … → 2059 messages). The run can never recover on its own.

### Evidence (session JSONL + fa.log, host of record, 2026-10-18)

1. **The model enforces a hard per-request MESSAGE-ARRAY cap of 2048**, independent of token count. `model_request_summary` records show the message count climbing by 2 per turn (tool call + result) to 2049 by 08:21, with every subsequent heartbeat at +2: 2051, 2053, 2055, 2057, 2059. The first 400 lands at exactly 2049.
2. **The session was token-healthy at the time.** The last successful compaction (07:07, `auto-compact pass 3 fallback=structured·hide-fallback tokens 20023→130354 ok=true`) had reduced tokens to ~130k of a 200k window — well under the token trigger. The message array, however, kept growing because the agent ran ~7 tool calls/minute (bash/read/write every ~10s in fa.log).
3. **fa context management is token-only by design** (`lib/src/compaction/compaction.dart` header: "The pipeline is token-based, never message-count-based"; the mid-turn over-window guard in `agent_loop.dart:1476` measures `estimateRequestTokens` vs `window`). There is no message-count dimension anywhere.
4. **The 400 is not classified as overflow.** `lib/src/overflow.dart` `_overflowPatterns` covers token-based overflow errors ("prompt is too long", "exceeds the context window", "too many tokens", "context length exceeded", …) but has **no pattern for `array length N exceeds limit M`** → `isContextOverflow` returns false. The 400 is also not rate-limit/transient → it is terminal per attempt.
5. **No error-driven context repair exists.** The loop's `over-window relief` (issue #387) and the auto-compactor fire only on TOKEN thresholds. A provider-side context refusal (this 400) is not a compaction/trim trigger — the run wedges.
6. **Compounding factor — compaction judge timeout on the same gateway (issue #515).** At 07:07 auto-compact pass 2 failed: `compaction judge timeout (role=smol, model=zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash @ gate.joingonka.ai, 300s budget)`. The smol judge timed out; the fallback bounds by tokens (`keepRecentTokens`), never by message count — so even a successful compaction cannot pull the array under a message cap.

### Root cause (fixable harness defects)

- **A. No message-count awareness.** The model's message-array cap is not modeled; compaction, the over-window guard, and local-trim are all token-only.
- **B. Overflow classifier misses the cap-400.** `overflow.dart` needs a pattern for `array length N exceeds limit M`.
- **C. A provider context refusal never triggers a self-healing repair.** The pairing-400 repair exists (`agent_loop.dart:1489`, issue #85) but a message-cap 400 does not; nothing coalesces/compacts the array under the cap and retries.

---

## Goal — adaptive per-model message-cap handling: learn the cap from the error, coalesce + compact on refusal, trigger compaction before the cap (v2)

**A run can never wedge on a provider message-count cap: the cap is learned per model from the provider's own error, a cap refusal coalesces and compacts the context, and once learned, compaction fires before the cap is reached — with zero hardcoded provider/model tables.**

v1 of this card modeled `maxMessages` as a per-provider tuning knob. The user's correction: JoinGonka is a **gateway hosting many models**, each with its own limit — the cap is a property of the **model**, not the endpoint, and hardcoding provider/model tables is exactly what must not happen. The cap must be **discovered from the error text and learned per model**, then used as a **message-count compaction trigger**.

## Why this framing (supersedes v1)

- Retracted: `maxMessages` as a per-provider/baseUrl tuning entry — wrong granularity (one gateway, many models) and wrong source (hardcoded).
- Retracted: "pinned cap in the catalog" — the only built-in knowledge is the error-text classifier; the cap value itself is learned.
- Chosen: **learn by example, act pre-emptively**. The classifier recognizes the cap-400 shape (built-in, tiny, provider-agnostic); the specific limit `M` is parsed from the error and stored per model identity `(provider, modelId)`; a subsequent run compacts before the cap instead of after the failure.

## Architecture

```
request → cap-400 "array length 2049 exceeds limit 2048"
   │  overflow.dart classifier (NEW pattern; parses M=2048)
   ▼
learn: store (provider, modelId) → maxMessages=M        [persisted per-model store]
   ▼
repair (reactive): coalesce old tool-call/result pairs → send STRAIGHT to a compaction pass
   → retry once
   ▼
next runs (pre-emptive): before each request,
   messageCount ≥ learnedCap − margin  ⇒  trigger compaction (message-count trigger)
   → request rides a compacted array, never a doomed round-trip
```

- **Cap discovery** — `overflow.dart` gains the classifier for `array length N exceeds limit M` / `messages: … exceeds limit …` (and returns the parsed `M`). Provider-agnostic: any model that emits this shape is handled; the regex is the ONLY built-in.
- **Learned-cap store** — a per-model record keyed `(provider, modelId) → maxMessages`, persisted next to the existing per-provider `model_cache.json` lifecycle (boot-load + background warm-refresh; same file family or a sibling). No provider/model tables in source.
- **Reactive repair (first occurrence)** — on a classified cap-400: **coalesce** the outbound array (merge adjacent tool-call/result pairs and old turns into compact messages — the user's "объединить сообщения"), then **send straight to a compaction pass** (the summary is the real message-count reducer), then retry once. A second cap-400 surfaces the terminal error.
- **Pre-emptive trigger (after learning)** — the auto-compactor gains a message-count trigger in addition to the token trigger: `messageCount ≥ learnedCap − margin` fires compaction BEFORE the request. Additive; the token trigger is untouched.

Invariants:
- Coalesce/compact never drops the newest user message or the system prompt; only whole tool-call/result pairs older than the cut point go.
- The session JSONL is byte-identical — repair is outbound-only (like `rewriteHistoryImages` and the pairing repair).
- The only hardcoded knowledge is the error-text classifier; no provider/model name appears in source.
- A model with no learned cap behaves byte-identically to today.

## Capability surface

| Capability | Subject | Shape | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cap-400 classifier | the provider error string | overflow.dart pattern for `array length N exceeds limit M` (+ variants), exposing parsed `M` | core |
| Learned per-model cap | the model identity `(provider, modelId)` | persisted record → `maxMessages`; boot-loaded; no hardcoded tables | core |
| Reactive repair | the outbound messages array | cap-400 → coalesce + compaction pass → retry once | core |
| Pre-emptive compaction trigger | the outbound messages array | `messageCount ≥ learnedCap − margin` fires compaction before the request | core |
| Coalesce step | the outbound messages array | merge adjacent tool-call/result pairs + old turns into compact messages (pairing-safe) | core |
| Cap notice | the user/UI | a trim/compaction fired by the cap names the cap and the count (no values) | core |
| Config override | a model's learned cap | user can pin/edit a model's cap in config (overrides the learned value) | second tier |
| Hardcoded cap tables | — | exclud…

The new `overCap` term correctly fires the pass, but the gate's final verdict a few lines below is still:

```dart
return after <= _effectiveContextWindow;
```

— judged purely on tokens. When the cap dimension triggered the pass and the transcript still rides at/above `cap − margin` after compaction (recent messages can't be hidden), the gate reports success and the CLI sends a still-over-cap request: one doomed provider round-trip per turn until the reactive heal coalesces the retry. The `AutoCompactor` itself already reports `success: ... && !_overMessageCap()`; consider mirroring the message-count check in this return (e.g. `&& !messageCapTriggerReached(_agent.state.messages.length, _modelCaps.learnedCapFor(_agent.state.model))`) so an unfixable-over-cap pass reads as failure instead of silently re-arming every turn.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-18):

💡 **SUGGESTION: second-tier pin API shipped with zero callers**

`pin()`, `remove()`, and `learnedCapOr()` (and the pin-semantics paragraph on `learnFromRefusal`) implement the ticket's "second tier: config override" — but nothing in the tree calls them: no config key, no `/`-command, no host wiring, and the pre-emptive gate reads only the raw learned value. Either wire the override (even minimally, e.g. a `modelCaps` map in config consulted via `learnedCapOr` in `_messageCapPolicy`) or drop the API from this PR and add it with the follow-up that uses it — dead public surface in a fresh module rots fast.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-18):

💡 **SUGGESTION: E1 deviation — cap-unknown models never get the pre-emptive pass the ticket specifies**

The ticket's edge case E1 says: cap error without a parseable number → "the model is flagged cap-unknown → **pre-emptive compaction fires on the next request** (one pass), then retry". This line instead arms no coalesce target, and since `learnedCapFor` returns null for a cap-unknown record, `messageCapTriggerReached` never fires pre-emptively either — a cap-unknown model is healed *reactively* (relief + retry per refusal) instead. That still satisfies the hard requirement (never a wedge), but it diverges from the ticket's specified mechanism: every refusal costs a full refused round-trip plus a compaction pass, forever. Consider either giving cap-unknown records a conservative pre-emptive trigger (e.g. fire on the next request after each refusal, as E1 words it) or noting the deliberate deviation on the issue so the edge case isn't re-litigated later.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-18):

💡 **SUGGESTION: clamp `learnedCap - margin` against pathological small caps**

`count >= learnedCap - margin` is unclamped: a learned cap at or below the default margin of 16 (a provider with a tiny per-request array cap, or a misparse like `array length 4 exceeds limit 8` variants) makes `learnedCap - margin` ≤ 0, so the trigger is **always** true — the pre-emptive pass fires on every turn, can never satisfy its own success criterion, and the session lives in a permanent compact-every-turn state. mergeable solo unit. When the pairing scan hits a non-matching message before

blocks.text:
# crap4dart configuration for flutter_agent_harness.
# https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart
#
# RATCHET: the CRAP threshold is pinned at the current worst score
# (356.34, `_handleKey` in bin/../tui_repl.dart) — pushes may only make
# the codebase BETTER, never worse. Lower the threshold whenever the top
# offenders are fixed (run: dart pub global run crap4dart analyze).

sources: [lib, bin]

exclude:
  - '**.g.dart'
  - '**.freezed.dart'
  - '**.mocks.dart'
  - 'build/**'
  - 'vendor/**'

crap:
  enabled: true
  # Current max CRAP score in the repo: 12.0 (re-measured whole-tree on
  # the merged-suite lcov, #1234 rework). The card's named offenders DID
  # move — readPasteboardImage 16.32 (split into fake-seam /
  # platform-dispatch helpers), the CC-12 trio (_handleTreeKey,
  # discoverTaskAgents, _rebuild) split into cohesive sub-dispatchers,
  # the four 0%-cov CC-3 methods covered by tests (frontmatter, video
  # endpoint, below-window ingest, provider picker), the named CC-9 tier
  # split, and _listModels (20 @ 0%) covered by the line-mode /models
  # test. But the FIRST real whole-tree measurement (the authoring box
  # had no dart toolchain) shows the 12.0 → 8.0 repin is not earned yet:
  # 137 methods measure above 8.0 — 54 at exactly 12.00 (the CC-3 @ 0%
  # tier + fully-covered CC-12 dispatchers) and 83 at 9.00 (CC-9 @ 100%).
  # Threshold stays at the measured max; the 12.00/9.00 tier is the next
  # ladder card (cover the CC-3@0% half, split the CC-12 dispatchers,
  # then the threshold follows down to 8.0). Only down from here.
  threshold: 12.0
  # _listModels used to hit 20 with 0% coverage (line-mode-only output);
  # covered by test/cli/provider_models_line_mode_test.dart in #1234.

# ─── loc gate (issue #1234, gh-1232 migration) ─────────────────────────────
# The ≤2800-line file guard MOVED from scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_size +
# the ci.yml shell find-exec guards onto crap4dart's `loc` gate (0.11.0,
# maintainer-confirmed wc -l semantics). Enforced whole-tree on every merge
# validation via `crap4dart check --baseline` (CI quality-gates step) and
# staged files in the pre-commit hook — no staged-scoping escape, no
# hook-dependence, merge-bot merges included. max_lines only DOWN;
# app_localizations.dart is gen-l10n OUTPUT (no .g.dart suffix) — excluded,
# not baselined.

coverage:
  # scripts/pre-commit regenerates this (dart test --coverage) right
  # before the CRAP step runs.
  lcov_path: coverage/lcov.info
  required: true
  branch_coverage: true
  # crap4dart 0.9.5 flipped the run_tests default to true — a bare
  # `analyze`/`check` would silently re-run the whole core suite first.
  # Coverage is regenerated explicitly (pre-commit hook, CI shard merge);
  # do not pay for it twice.
  run_tests: false

# ─── Gates (issue #447) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 0.9.5 default-enables ALL built-in gates; only broken_goldens is
# enforced here, everything else is disabled explicitly so a bare
# `check --staged` (pre-commit, core-only #433 split) means exactly the
# pixel gate. The flutter_app goldens live in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
gates:
  # Issue #1234: the whole-tree ≤2800-line guard (was stage_size +
  # ci.yml shell find-exec, gh-1232). wc -l semantics, generated output
  # excluded — nothing exceeds 2800 today, so the shrink-only baseline
  # starts EMPTY of loc entries. Scope = the package sources [lib, bin]:
  # 0.11.0 has NO per-gate sources override (gates.loc.sources is a
  # ConfigException — caught by CI on 019ede65), and the top-level
  # sources drive the CRAP census too, so they stay untouched. test/ and
  # example/ are enforced by the companion config
  # crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml (same loc gate, sources [test, example]);
  # the app package's own config covers flutter_app/lib.
  loc:
    enabled: true
    max_lines: 2800
    exclude:
      - '**.g.dart'
      - '**.freezed.dart'
      - '**.mocks.dart'
      - 'vendor/**'
  test_coverage: {enabled: false} # own ≥80% coverage-gate job
  complexity: {enabled: false} # CRAP ratchet above already covers it
  method_size: {enabled: false}
  nesting: {enabled: false}
  class_size: {enabled: false}
  weight_of_class: {enabled: false}
  unused_code: {enabled: false}
  unused_files: {enabled: false} # follow-up card (issue #1234 §5). Known
    # FPs to exclude when enabling: the conditional-export IO entry points
    # (lib/io.dart, lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart — public barrels whose
    # importers live outside this repo's import graph) and shared pinned
    # data modules imported only from test/ (lib/src/cli/omp_reg_scenarios.dart,
    # issue #810). lib/fanet.dart was the one confirmed-dead hit — deleted
    # in #1234.
  banned_imports: {enabled: false}
  # Type-2 duplication gate (issue #1106, crap4dart 0.11.0). Renamed-clone
  # detection on top of the Type-1 default; the union with the raw pass can
  # only ADD findings, never lose exact copies. severity: warning starts
  # soft — escalate to error once the 13-file triage debt is paid
  # (follow-up, owner-side). The global jscpd <1% guards stay as-is.
  #
  # Two suppression channels with different contracts:
  # - `// crap:ignore` (needs ignorable: true) = a JUSTIFIED structural
  #   twin, suppressed forever, with a one-line reason in the comment.
  # - `.crap-baseline.json` (via `check --baseline`) = LEGACY debt; the
  #   committed snapshot must only SHRINK: after each triage batch re-run
  #   `dart pub global run crap4dart check --save-baseline` and commit the
  #   only-down diff, or the snapshot rots and starts masking shifts.
  #
  # WINDOW (until severity flips to error): the gate never fails a build —
  # new (not-baselined) duplication only surfaces as a `[WARN]` line in
  # `check` output. Enforcement becomes hard exactly when the owner-side
  # escalation lands; from then on any finding outside the two channels
  # fails CI/pre-commit.
  duplication:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    ignorable: true # enables `// crap:ignore` for justified structural twins
    ignore_locals: true # Type-2: rename locals before hashing (API names stay)
    ignore_literals: false # keeps l10n/theme/symbol tables out
    sources: # cross-module scope from #487
      - flutter_app/lib
      - packages/fa_ui/lib
      - packages/fa_llm/lib
  file_naming: {enabled: false}
  magic_constants: {enabled: false}
  test_assertions: {enabled: false}
  folder_structure: {enabled: false}
  external: {enabled: false}
  public_docs: {enabled: false}
  golden: {enabled: false} # flutter-only gate (core is not a Flutter project)
  accessibility: {enabled: false}
  hardcoded_strings: {enabled: false}

  # Pixel gate over core test/ goldens — none exist today, so this is a
  # no-op that guards the future (issue #447 AC: "and core test/ goldens
  # if any appear"). WARNING, same rationale as flutter_app: the 0.9.5
  # detector misses the Ahem-solid-rect and hollow-square classes and
  # false-positives on V-converging shapes; flip to error when the
  # upstream detector fixes land.
  broken_goldens:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    dirs: [test]
    exclude:
      # TUI screenshots, not goldens: amber/yellow text on the dark theme
      # trips the stripe heuristic (measured 14/14 "overflow stripes" —
      # the same yellow-on-dark detector bug the issue documents for
      # apps_panel/panel_dark). Revisit when upstream fixes land.
      - 'test/integration/**'

The guards job runs:
1. `crap4dart analyze` — CRAP ratchet with threshold 12.0, requires coverage/lcov.info (coverage.required: true). CI merges shard lcov into coverage/lcov.info. Locally I don't have that. But CRAP score with no coverage would treat everything as 0% covered → scores skyrocket → ratchet would fail... but coverage required:true would error if missing.
2. `crap4dart check --baseline` — gates: loc (max 280) + duplication (warning severity — never fails) + broken_goldens (warning). Hmm, with severity warning, gates don't fail. But baseline check: `.crap-baseline.json` must only shrink? "the committed snapshot must only SHRINK" — maybe check --baseline fails if baseline entries no longer match or if new findings exist.

What changed in this PR? +2390 lines across 24 files. New files: lib/src/agent/message_cap.dart etc. Possible failure causes:
- A new file exceeding 280 lines? Unlikely with new ~small files.
- CRAP threshold exceeded: a new method with CRAP > 12.0 (with real coverage from shards).
- Duplication gate: new Type-2 clones flagged — but severity warning, never fails.
- The CRAP ratchet `analyze` with the merged lcov: a changed method's CRAP exceeding 12.0.

Also the duplication guard jscpd <1% on lib/ — that's a step in guards too ("Duplication guard (lib/ < 1%)"). New code could push duplication ≥1%.

# contexts (shard 0..3) never report, and branch protection blocks
    # out-of-scope PRs at 27 green checks. The scope fastpass below
    # green-skips the real steps in seconds instead.
    name: Core tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    timeout-minutes: 12
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared changes — shard green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')

`coalesceMessagesForCap` has CC 17. CRAP = CC² × (1 − cov)³ = 289 × (1−cov)³. Threshold 12. So even at 90% coverage: 289×0.001=0.29 — fine. At 80% coverage: 289×0.008=2.3. The danger zone is coverage < ~40%: at cov 0% → 289 FAIL. The coalesce test file has 258 lines of tests covering several scenarios; but CC 17 means many branches — partial coverage could leave CRAP > 12 if coverage < ~42% (289×(1-cov)³ > 12 → (1-cov)³ > 0.0415 → 1-cov > 0.346 → cov < 65.4%). Wait recompute: (1-cov)^3 > 12/289 = 0.04152 → 1-cov > 0.346 → cov < 65.4%. So if coalesceMessagesForCap coverage is below ~65%, CRAP > 12 → ratchet fails.

Hmm, but branch_coverage: true — branch coverage is typically lower. CRAP uses method coverage (function-level?) or line coverage? crap4dart uses the coverage % of the method — with branch_coverage true it might use branch coverage, which is usually much lower than line coverage! If coalesce's branch coverage is, say, 55%, CRAP = 289 × 0.45³ = 26.4 → FAIL. That's very plausibly the root cause.

So the fix: reduce complexity of coalesceMessagesForCap (split into helpers) and/or add tests to cover branches. TDD: write tests to raise coverage; and refactor to lower CC.

Let's wait for the coverage run to confirm precisely which methods exceed 12.0. Meanwhile inspect other suspects: `_maybeAutoCompact` CC7 (49×(1-cov)³; fails if cov<~9%... at cov 0 → 49 > 12!). _capResumedContext CC7, onPass CC8 (64), formatCompactionReport CC7, _maybeOverWindowContinue CC8, _guardCheckpointRestoreBudget CC9 (81!). Any of these at low coverage fails. But these are mostly pre-existing functions except the modified ones (_maybeAutoCompact, _capResumedContext, onPass maybe modified).

Once the suite finishes, format lcov and run analyze to get the exact offenders. Wait for the job.
